heading: Complaint Categories
text: The Smart Panchayat Portal accepts complaints in the following categories: Water, Electricity, Road, Sanitation, Street Light, Drainage, and Other. - Water: drinking water supply, pipeline leaks, water quality, borewell and tank issues. - Electricity: power cuts, transformer problems, damaged poles, exposed wiring, meter issues. - Road: potholes, road damage, missing dividers, missing speed breakers. - Sanitation: uncollected garbage, public toilet

When you submit a complaint, the portal's AI classifier suggests a category based on your description, but you can always pick a different category yourself before submitting. heading: Complaint Status Workflow
text: Every complaint moves through a status field that can be one of: Submitted, Under Review, Assigned, In Progress, Resolved, or Rejected. - Submitted: the complaint has been received by the portal. This is the automatic starting status the moment you submit the form. - Under Review: a Panchayat officer or admin is looking into the complaint to verify details before

text: Review: a Panchayat officer or admin is looking into the complaint to verify details before acting on it. - Assigned: the complaint has been assigned to a specific officer or department for action. - In Progress: work on resolving the complaint has started. - Resolved: the issue has been fixed and the complaint is closed. - Rejected: the complaint was

heading: Possibly Related or Duplicate Complaints
text: When an officer or admin opens a complaint for review, the portal shows a list of other complaints in the same category that are textually similar to it, based on an AI similarity score. This is meant to help staff notice when several citizens are reporting the same underlying issue (for example, the same broken street light reported by different

heading: Possibly Related or Duplicate Complaints

The portal does **not** automatically merge, delete, or close complaints it flags as similar — an officer or admin must review the flagged complaints and decide manually whether to link or act on them together. heading: Escalation and Contact
text: If you are not satisfied with how your complaint has been handled, the best first step is to check its current status and history on the "Track Complaint" page — an officer may have already left a status update explaining what's happening. heading: How to Submit a Complaint
text: 1. Log in to your citizen account and go to "Submit Complaint". 2. Enter a short title for your complaint. 3. Write a description of the problem. heading: Priority Levels
text: Complaints can have one of three priority levels: Low, Medium, or High. Priority affects how urgently a complaint is expected to be handled by Panchayat officers, but it does not change what category the complaint belongs to. heading: Tracking Your Complaint and Resolution-Time Estimates
text: You can track any complaint you've submitted from the "Track Complaint" page, which shows the current status and the full history of status changes with timestamps. If your complaint is still open (not Resolved or Rejected), the page also shows an AI-estimated resolution time in days.
